quote: “To will oneself free is also to will others free.”
source: Simone de Beauvoir, The Ethics of Ambiguity, Part II, Personal Freedom and Others (trans. Bernard Frechtman, 1948)

evidence.where: Marxists Internet Archive transcription of the Frechtman translation (credited there: translated by Bernard Frechtman, Citadel Press printing), chapter page for Part II, Personal Freedom and Others; the sentence is in the closing paragraph of that part, between the words incapable of proposing any content to the freedom which it wants engaged and This will is not an abstract formula.
evidence.edition: The Ethics of Ambiguity, trans. Bernard Frechtman (Philosophical Library, 1948; Citadel Press, 1949)
evidence.locator: Part II, Personal Freedom and Others, final paragraph

reason: Exact wording of the Frechtman translation, located in Part II as proposed. Simone de Beauvoir has one line in the year (month 1), under the cap and not yet in this month; not banned; nothing shipped.
